threatModel.summary: Generated source-backed model of current /Users/arthrod/temp/T/jubarte-redlines, scope ., observed live HEAD 4e10eca69c42211651ca907f38b74b6d19e6928c. Jubarte is a local Rust DOCX compare/edit/validate/inspect/scrub/render engine with legacy DOC and Markdown conversion; bytes flow through Rust APIs, PyO3, wasm-bindgen, native/Python/Node CLIs and optional stdio MCP (src/lib.rs:7-36; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:5-15; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:7-28; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:373-381). Conditional privileged workflows are explicit native self-update and maintainer release publication.
assets: Document bytes/text/revisions/comments/authors/metadata, PDF/PNG output, edit reports; MCP read tools return content while edit/render publish derived files (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-150,185-218,229-255).

Worker CPU/memory during ZIP/XML/comparison/image/font processing. InputLimits defaults 64 MiB compressed/per part, 256 MiB inflated, 10000 entries and depth 256; comparison uses 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB inflated (src/admission.rs:63-99).

Document/export confinement under the operator-selected MCP root; native CLI has ambient local authority. Publication stages and verifies all files, then commits atomically per file, not across the set (src/publication.rs:146-225).
Ambient font files, persistent font-index paths and sibling temporary cache files outside document roots (src/convert/font.rs:2258-2275,2637-2652,3100-3107,3183-3188,3213-3229).

Installed executable integrity and release/package identities. Signing keys are secret references decoded into temporary runner files; publishing token is separate (.github/workflows/release.yml:261-309,356-369; src/update.rs:198-210).
trustBoundaries: Document supplier -> in-process package admission -> XML/DOM/media consumers. Admission checks declared/streamed budgets, duplicate names and ZIP defects; comparison admits both active-setting inputs (src/admission.rs:439-470; src/document_comparer.rs:6530-6567). Ordinary budgets and comparison budgets differ (src/admission.rs:63-99).

Raw XML caller -> checked try_parse_xdocument_with_limits versus intentionally permissive parse_xdocument. Checked parsing validates before construction; permissive parsing requires caller gating (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:84-135).

MCP --root defaults cwd -> expanduser/resolve once -> native _OutputRoot -> retained cap-std directory. Consumer document read effective path <root>/<client-relative input>; output edit effective paths <root>/<out_dir>/{clean.docx,redline.docx,patch.diff,report.json,optional redline.pdf/redline-page-NN.png}; render outputs <root>/<out_dir>/{page-NN.png,optional render.pdf}. Python containment is diagnostic; native capability-relative reads/publish enforce actual I/O, overwrite is explicit (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,170-255,373-381; src/publication.rs:146-199).

All connected stdio MCP callers share exposed tool authority. Read/write annotations are descriptive, not independent authentication or tool-level authorization (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,126-159,373-381).

Native CLI explicit destinations -> publish_paths(root=None) -> ambient OS filesystem permissions, staged verified replacement. Node CLI explicit paths -> fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync with existsSync precheck; it does not inherit native publication guarantees (src/bin/jubarte.rs:261-273; src/publication.rs:203-225; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:52-79,106-111,137-145).

Native document font requests -> ambient lookup: nonempty JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides user directory; defaults macOS $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, Linux ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/jubarte/fonts, Windows $APPDATA/jubarte/fonts; installed/Word/cloud directories also searched. Recipients are native font parsers and renderer; OS permissions apply independently of MCP root (src/convert/font.rs:2258-2275,2281-2315,2637-2652).

Native persistent index consumer: JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX explicit path wins; empty/off disables; absent -> parent(user_font_dir)/font-index.tsv. Effective defaults macOS $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/font-index.tsv, Linux ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/jubarte/font-index.tsv, Windows $APPDATA/jubarte/font-index.tsv; JUBARTE_FONT_DIR changes default to its parent's index. Cache is consumed by subsequent renderer processes under OS permissions; save writes sibling path.with_extension(tsv.<pid>.tmp), then renames (src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652,3100-3112,3154-3188,3192-3229).

Explicit updater -> fixed jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines release and supported platform -> selected tag -> SHA256SUMS.txt -> archive child jubarte-<version>-<platform>-<arch>/jubarte[.exe] -> delegated executable install. Terminal/--yes preflight, check-only mode, checksum and regular-file hook enforce separate controls. RELEASE_KEYS=[] and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE=None mean signatures are not currently required (src/update.rs:25-48,87-108,120-125,186-257,299-310).

Tag-driven maintainer release -> five native targets -> dist/jubarte-*.tar.gz or .zip. secrets.ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY -> signing-step environment -> base64 decode -> $RUNNER_TEMP/zipsign.XXXXXX/keyN -> zipsign; 64-byte key check, cleanup trap and committed-key verification; optional secret only when no public keys committed. SHA256SUMS.txt generated after signing. secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN -> GH_TOKEN -> gh release create github.repository/GITHUB_REF_NAME with notes.md and dist/* (.github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,58-144,261-322,356-369).
scripts/release.sh registry publication uses maintainer cargo/npm/uv credentials independently of document processing (scripts/release.sh:370-380,878-919,924-959,1069-1070).
attackerCapabilities: Document adversary supplies ZIP entries, XML, relationship targets, images/fonts and content chosen for processing by a victim. No assumption of control over host environment, MCP root, outside filesystem, release accounts or signing keys.

Connected MCP client invokes all granted tools and selects root-relative documents/outputs, including overwrite=true. Root selection is operator authority; no remotely authenticated or multi-tenant deployment is established (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,152-159,373-381).

Document-only attacker must not gain arbitrary host file access, outbound fetching, executable installation or writes outside authorized destinations. Representative relationship consumers distinguish External targets from package bytes instead of fetching them; this is not exhaustive no-network proof (src/document_comparer.rs:100-108; src/opc/mod.rs:766-783).

Release-asset adversary has a separate capability from a document supplier. Current checksum-only update depends on release-hosting and TLS integrity; signature separation from release-asset control is inactive (src/update.rs:44-48,245-257; docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:69-87).
securityObjectives: Enforce active archive and XML limits before expensive processing and require checked raw XML or prior admission (src/admission.rs:63-99,439-470; src/xmllinq/parse.rs:84-135).

Keep MCP document reads and exports under retained directory capability, reject unsafe names/conflicts and accurately report partial commit/durability outcomes; retain distinction from native ambient CLI and Node direct writes (src/publication.rs:146-225; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:76-79,106-111).

Require explicit updater/install authority, bind platform/version/member, checksum and extracted file type; communicate current absence of signature enforcement (src/update.rs:87-108,120-125,198-257,299-310).

Constrain signing credentials to intended release step and avoid disclosure in artifacts/reports; actual hosted secret values and runner permissions are external facts (.github/workflows/release.yml:261-309,356-369).

Treat admission budgets as controls rather than complete process isolation. Embedders choose tighter CPU/memory budgets; WASM documentation recommends lowering the 2 GiB comparison budget for browser hosts (jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:77-85; src/admission.rs:80-99).
assumptions: Model reflects explicitly supplied live target, not revision in scan directory name. No deployment, tenant model, listener, container mapping or actual environment supplied; paths are symbolic code-derived values.

Documentation disagreement retained: MCP says every path/output/tool operation is under --root (jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:5-9,67-82), whereas native rendering reads ambient fonts and writes the independently configured index outside it (src/convert/font.rs:2258-2275,2637-2652,3100-3107,3183-3188,3213-3229). This qualifies global claim without itself proving arbitrary document-directed file access.
Documentation disagreement retained: src/lib.rs:7-11 says no temp files; enabled native font-index persistence writes sibling tsv.<pid>.tmp then renames (src/convert/font.rs:3213-3229).
docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:69-87 accurately documents current conditional-signing/checksum-only bootstrap. Feature support alone does not establish enforcement (src/update.rs:44-48,245-257).
docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:22-24 names GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN, but builder passes no explicit token (src/update.rs:198-211); dependency automatic environment behavior remains unverified.

Host OS permissions, cap-std platform internals, decoder internals, updater dependency transport/extraction, release job exact token scope and actual hosted secret state require separate verification where material. No runtime application execution, network requests or vulnerability-triggering inputs.

Root SECURITY.md is analysis context, including external-relationship no-fetch claim, raw parser caller obligation and process memory/CPU recommendation. Architecture mapping alone is not completed security audit coverage.

findings.title: Untrusted table spans cause unbounded renderer allocations
findings.summary: A small DOCX table can set w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter to a large usize. The shared PDF/PNG layout pipeline admits the package, derives column occupancy from these values, and allocates column and merge vectors at that size without a semantic budget. This can exhaust worker memory or panic before returning a normal conversion error. The HTML altChunk importer also accepts unbounded colspan and emits one gridCol per logical column.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can deterministically deny service to a process rendering the supplied file with very small input. Impact is availability of that process; no remote service or broader compromise is assumed, and process resource limits constrain host-wide impact.

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace from public conversion entry points through admission and uncapped attribute parsing to Vec allocation; no runtime exploit was executed.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled resource allocation from untrusted document metadata

codeEvidence.label: Cell span lacks an upper bound
codeEvidence.explanation: The return type (usize, VMerge) makes the parsed span an attacker-controlled usize; max(1) sets only a minimum.

codeEvidence.label: Row skips use the same uncapped span
codeEvidence.explanation: gridBefore and gridAfter create RawCell placeholders with this span and enter the same occupancy calculation.

codeEvidence.label: Occupancy directly sizes column allocations
codeEvidence.explanation: For one cell with span 1073741824, this attempts a 4 GiB f32 column vector before other span-sized allocations.

codeEvidence.label: Merge tracking also allocates by span
codeEvidence.code:
if open.len() < col + span {
                open.resize(col + span, None);
codeEvidence.explanation: The same metadata controls a second potentially much larger per-column vector.

codeEvidence.label: Renderer admits input before layout
codeEvidence.explanation: This establishes the real untrusted package boundary. Existing archive/XML size/depth limits do not constrain numeric grid values.

codeEvidence.label: HTML colspan has no upper bound
codeEvidence.code:
self.cell_spans.push(
                    attr(open, "colspan")
                        .and_then(|s| s.trim().parse::<usize>().ok())
                        .unwrap_or(1)
                        .max(1),
codeEvidence.explanation: The same missing semantic-column budget affects HTML colspans before table DOM construction.

codeEvidence.label: One XML element emitted per logical column
codeEvidence.explanation: end_table computes cols as maximum sum of cell.span (469-475) and emits unchecked attacker-sized output.

rootCause.summary: The renderer accepts cell spans and row skips as unbounded machine integers and expands sparse semantic counts into dense vectors without checked cumulative arithmetic or an allocation budget. The sibling HTML importer lacks the same column budget and performs span-sized XML emission.

findings.remediation: Apply a conservative semantic maximum to cell spans, row skips and cumulative grid columns before creating RawCell or allocating vectors. Use checked cumulative arithmetic and return a typed resource-limit error before any span-derived loop/allocation. Enforce the same budget in every shared layout path. Apply this semantic maximum during HTML colspan parsing and table emission as well.

counterEvidence: Package admission enforces byte, ZIP entry, XML depth and attribute limits before layout; those checks accept short decimal span attributes.
stretch_stale_spans returns early when used spans exceed existing columns (14172-14177); it does not cap spans.
SECURITY.md recommends process CPU/memory isolation; that mitigates host impact but does not prevent termination of a rendering worker.
limitations: No application code executed; no claim of a deployed remotely accessible renderer.
validation.summary: Validated by reading the public PDF/render entry points (422-460,592-645), with_layout admission (769-799), table_block callers (8619,9178,17184,20598), span propagation (13200-13216,13466,13530-13536), allocation (13600-13619) and merge tracking (14600-14644). InputLimits fields (src/admission.rs:42-60) cover byte/entry/XML structural limits, not grid counts. Parent additionally validated HTML colspan parsing (altchunk.rs:562-566), sum (469-475) and 0..cols emission (489-490).

controls: Host-enforced process resource limits recommended by SECURITY.md

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> public docx_to_pdf/render -> with_layout -> admitted main-part DOM -> table_block -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy/merge vectors.

impact.rationale: Memory exhaustion, capacity panic or excessive work in rendering process.

likelihood.rationale: Large positive numeric table spans require no optional unsafe parser or elevated caller authority once rendering occurs.

reachability.summary: Public Rust PDF and raster conversion accept caller-provided DOCX bytes and share this layout path. A tiny ordinary table with one large positive span reaches allocation without exceeding byte/depth admission limits.
reachability.attacker: Supplier of a document rendered by another caller
preconditions: Victim renders an attacker-supplied DOCX containing a table.

attackPath.summary: An untrusted document supplier gains denial of service of the process that renders their table.

remediationTests: Test default public PDF and PNG/render entry points with small DOCX tables containing excessive gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter values; require typed refusal before allocation.
Test cumulative multi-cell spans and machine-width boundary values, plus legitimate merged tables within the budget.

originalCandidates.title: Unbounded table grid spans cause renderer allocations
originalCandidates.evidence: DOCX renderer trusts w:gridSpan and w:gridBefore/gridAfter as usize (src/convert/mod.rs:14211-14215,14340-14346), then sums spans and allocates cols of occupancy (13599-13615), and merge tracking resizes to col+span (14637-14638). A tiny admitted document with gridSpan=1073741824 drives multi-GB allocation; usize::MAX causes capacity overflow panic. Entry/control context and sibling investigation pending.

baselineReturnedCandidate.title: Unbounded table spans cause attacker-sized allocations during rendering
baselineReturnedCandidate.attacker: An attacker supplying a DOCX rendered through Rust, Python, WASM or CLI conversion APIs.
baselineReturnedCandidate.violated_security_invariant: A small admitted document must not control allocation sizes independently of configured input budgets.

baselineReturnedCandidate.concrete_impact: Single-cell gridSpan=1073741824 requests at least 4 GiB f32 column vector then further proportional allocations; extreme values capacity-panic. HTML colspan=1073741824 emits over a billion XML elements.

Static review; no application/PoC execution

originalCandidates.title: Unbounded table grid spans cause renderer allocations
originalCandidates.evidence: DOCX renderer trusts w:gridSpan and w:gridBefore/gridAfter as usize (src/convert/mod.rs:14211-14215,14340-14346), then sums spans and allocates cols of occupancy (13599-13615), and merge tracking resizes to col+span (14637-14638). A tiny admitted document with gridSpan=1073741824 drives multi-GB allocation; usize::MAX causes capacity overflow panic. Entry/control context and sibling investigation pending.

previousFindings.title: Untrusted table spans cause unbounded renderer allocations
previousFindings.summary: A small DOCX table can set w:gridSpan, w:gridBefore or w:gridAfter to a large usize. The shared PDF/PNG layout pipeline admits the package, derives column occupancy from these values, and allocates column and merge vectors at that size without a semantic budget. This can exhaust worker memory or panic before returning a normal conversion error.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can deterministically deny service to a process rendering the supplied file with very small input. Impact is availability of that process; no remote service or broader compromise is assumed, and process resource limits constrain host-wide impact.

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace from public conversion entry points through admission and uncapped attribute parsing to Vec allocation; no runtime exploit was executed.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled resource allocation from untrusted document metadata

codeEvidence.label: Cell span lacks an upper bound
codeEvidence.explanation: The return type (usize, VMerge) makes the parsed span an attacker-controlled usize; max(1) sets only a minimum.

codeEvidence.label: Row skips use the same uncapped span
codeEvidence.explanation: gridBefore and gridAfter create RawCell placeholders with this span and enter the same occupancy calculation.

codeEvidence.label: Occupancy directly sizes column allocations
codeEvidence.explanation: For one cell with span 1073741824, this attempts a 4 GiB f32 column vector before other span-sized allocations.

codeEvidence.label: Merge tracking also allocates by span
codeEvidence.code:
if open.len() < col + span {
                open.resize(col + span, None);
codeEvidence.explanation: The same metadata controls a second potentially much larger per-column vector.

codeEvidence.label: Renderer admits input before layout
codeEvidence.explanation: This establishes the real untrusted package boundary. Existing archive/XML size/depth limits do not constrain numeric grid values.

rootCause.summary: The renderer accepts cell spans and row skips as unbounded machine integers and expands sparse semantic counts into dense vectors without checked cumulative arithmetic or an allocation budget.

previousFindings.remediation: Apply a conservative semantic maximum to cell spans, row skips and cumulative grid columns before creating RawCell or allocating vectors. Use checked cumulative arithmetic and return a typed resource-limit error before any span-derived loop/allocation. Enforce the same budget in every shared layout path.

counterEvidence: Package admission enforces byte, ZIP entry, XML depth and attribute limits before layout; those checks accept short decimal span attributes.
stretch_stale_spans returns early when used spans exceed existing columns (14172-14177); it does not cap spans.
SECURITY.md recommends process CPU/memory isolation; that mitigates host impact but does not prevent termination of a rendering worker.
limitations: No application code executed; no claim of a deployed remotely accessible renderer.
validation.summary: Validated by reading the public PDF/render entry points (422-460,592-645), with_layout admission (769-799), table_block callers (8619,9178,17184,20598), span propagation (13200-13216,13466,13530-13536), allocation (13600-13619) and merge tracking (14600-14644). InputLimits fields (src/admission.rs:42-60) cover byte/entry/XML structural limits, not grid counts.

controls: Host-enforced process resource limits recommended by SECURITY.md

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> public docx_to_pdf/render -> with_layout -> admitted main-part DOM -> table_block -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy/merge vectors.

impact.rationale: Memory exhaustion, capacity panic or excessive work in rendering process.

likelihood.rationale: Large positive numeric table spans require no optional unsafe parser or elevated caller authority once rendering occurs.

findings.title: Repeated altChunk references multiply content beyond admission budgets
findings.summary: The renderer admits original package bytes, then independently converts every HTML/MHT altChunk reference and concatenates the generated WML without an aggregate budget. Reusing one sizeable chunk thousands of times can generate gigabytes of XML before the unchecked DOM parser runs.

severity.rationale: A document supplier can exhaust a victim rendering process using compact input. Availability impact is deterministic once converted; no remote listener or host-wide compromise is assumed.

confidence.rationale: Original-entry admission and post-admission expansion loop directly establish multiplicative allocation/work. No runtime application code was executed.

taxonomy.category: Missing aggregate resource limit after content expansion

codeEvidence.label: Every occurrence converts and appends content
codeEvidence.explanation: expand's while rest.find("<w:altChunk") repeats this for every tag without limiting total generated bytes or occurrences.

codeEvidence.label: Expansion materializes after admission and before unchecked DOM
codeEvidence.explanation: Admission at 773-774 charges original archive entries. Embedded chunks are looked up in-memory and copies are expanded afterward; no transformed-byte re-admission occurs.

rootCause.summary: Resource admission charges each physical package part once, but the embedded-content transformation can repeatedly materialize that part without charging generated bytes or structural work.

findings.remediation: Apply an aggregate generated-byte and structural-work budget during HTML conversion and append, before intermediate outputs can grow past it. Bound reference expansion and cache conversion where useful; caching alone must not permit unlimited appends. Validate transformed XML with active policy before DOM construction.

counterEvidence: Archive entry and inflated bytes are bounded before expansion.
Only package part bytes are loaded, so this does not establish network or arbitrary file access.
Repeated tags may reuse the same relationship; no duplicate archive part/relationship is required.
Process memory/CPU limits mitigate host-wide impact; they do not bound generated XML.
limitations: No runtime triggering input or deployed service verified.
validation.summary: Parent verified expand (15-44), chunk loading/decoding, importer emission, original admission (admission.rs:516-554), with_layout ordering (mod.rs:773-798) and in-memory relationship lookup. A single text-rich 1MiB HTML chunk referenced 4096 times yields more than 4GiB generated XML without approaching original inflated-byte limits.

dataflow.summary: DOCX -> with_layout admission -> main XML -> expand -> per-reference load/chunk_html/html_to_wml -> aggregate String -> parse_xdocument.

impact.rationale: Worker termination or sustained resource consumption.

likelihood.rationale: Short repeated references amplify one admitted chunk through unconditional append.

reachability.summary: Public docx_to_pdf/render share with_layout and expand any main XML containing w:altChunk. Victim only needs to render the supplied package; no optional raised limits or external network fetching.

candidate.title: WMF records reconsume trailing file data
candidate.evidence: Rendering investigator: WMF polygon/polyline/text records read from whole data, never record slice, so tiny records can repeatedly parse huge trailing buffers. EMF sibling has record-bound checks. Exact dataflow and prerequisites pending.

returnedFinding.title: WMF record payloads escape declared boundaries, amplifying tiny records into large retained strings and geometry workloads
returnedFinding.attacker: Document provider controls embedded WMF referenced by DOCX converted to PDF/PNG.
returnedFinding.violated_security_invariant: Each metafile record must consume/allocate only its declared payload; repeated overlapping interpretation must be bounded.
returnedFinding.source_to_sink: resolve_media -> decode_image -> metafile::render -> raster_wmf validates declared record fits file but passes whole data to payload readers. TEXTOUT/EXTTEXTOUT strings and POLYGON/POLYPOLYGON/POLYLINE points extend through following records; outer off advances only declared size.
returnedFinding.concrete_impact: ~1MiB WMF with ~100000 eight-byte TEXTOUT records declaring 65535 bytes and sufficient trailing bytes (EOF before tail) retains multiple GiB overlapping strings. Eight-byte polygon/polyline with same point count causes billions of iterations. Static consequences, no execution.
supporting_source_evidence: size2 checked against data.len()-off, never data[off..off+size2]
size=4 words, n=65535 starts string in following record
POLYPOLYGON ring/point counts checked against full file
metafile renderer before ordinary image decoder limits
counterevidence: checked multiply/remaining size for outer record
canvas max384 per side, clipped strokes, widened polygon math
EMF read_emf_points checks off+size so confined WMF defect
Admission bytes and process limits do not bound repeated overlap/retention
No remote application/confidentiality exposure established
returnedFinding.recommended_remediation: Slice every WMF record to declared extent; check fixed fields, padded strings, ring/point arrays using checked math before allocation; reject malformed counts; aggregate decoded-text/geometry/work budgets; regress short TEXTOUT/EXTTEXTOUT/POLYGON/POLYPOLYGON/POLYLINE with tails.
